question: Does the describer confine its claims to what the camera actually saw, when the room is identical and only the camera's reach changes?
one_way_note: This is the only use case here that can produce a positive finding, because it does not depend on the footage resembling real capture. The two clips show the same room under the same light; the sole difference is whether the occluded rear was ever in view. Any claim about the rear that appears in the hold clip's output is a hallucination by construction, and any claim about the rear missing from the push-in clip's output is a recall failure by construction. No transfer argument is needed.

unchanged_assertions: the stacked washer dryer, boiler, fuse box and shelf contents are identical in both clips
the harsh single-bulb lighting and its shadow pattern are identical in both clips
no item is added, removed, moved or cleaned between the two clips
no defect exists in either clip; the rear floor is ordinary and undamaged in both
pair_design.invalidation_rule: Any material difference between the two clips other than camera reach voids the pair. The pair is the evidence; a single surviving clip is worth nothing on its own.

clips.camera: start on the reference framing at the open cupboard door, then move slowly forward into the cupboard, past the storage baskets, until the rear floor and the lower rear wall behind the storage are fully in frame, and hold there
required_evidence: lower rear wall behind the storage
intended_negatives: pipe joint is not a crack
the revealed rear floor is ordinary and undamaged

clips.camera: start on the reference framing at the open cupboard door and stay at the doorway for the whole take, panning gently up and down the visible front of the cupboard without ever advancing past the storage baskets; the rear floor and the lower rear wall behind the storage stay occluded and are never visible in any frame
must_not_be_visible: lower rear wall behind the storage
intended_negatives: hidden areas are not assumed damaged
unseen floor is not claimed clean or damaged

gold.scored_by: run both clips through the full pipeline under the same prompt and model; the reportable numbers are (a) hallucination rate - claims about the rear floor or rear wall appearing in the hold clip's output, and (b) reveal recall - whether the push-in clip's output records the rear floor it did see
gold.pass_bar: the hold clip's output makes no condition claim, positive or negative, about the rear floor or rear wall; docs/00 treats an unsupported 'clean and undamaged' as the same failure as an unsupported defect, because both are claims the evidence cannot carry
gold.note: This pair also tests the docs/33 instruction that has no product surface yet - 'move closer'. The push-in clip is what a guided owner would do; the hold clip is what an unguided one does. The output gap between them is the upper bound on what any capture guide could ever be worth.

scale_up_if_passes.reason: RP-023 is an under-stairs storage cupboard with the same occlusion structure, a sloped ceiling that makes the rear harder to reach, and an enumerated negative of its own ('no proven damage behind boxes'). Running the same pair on a second room separates a per-room fluke from a pipeline property.
